tool.name: mx_fingerprint
tool.description:
MX server fingerprint + sample-mail Authentication-Results analysis.
Two complementary checks for the email-recon story. Use during the recon phase for any `domain` target — pairs with `dns_hygiene_check` (which validates record presence) by fingerprinting what software is actually serving those records and how mail is actually authenticated downstream.
Behaviour:
1. **MX banner fingerprint.** Resolves the apex's MX records (up to 5 hosts, lowest-preference first). For each host, opens a single TCP connection to port 25, reads the SMTP greeting, sends EHLO, reads the response, sends QUIT. No STARTTLS, no auth, no message body.
2. **Sample-mail header analysis.** When `sample_email_path` is supplied — a local path to a saved `.eml` file from the target's domain — parses `Authentication-Results` to extract real-world SPF / DKIM / DMARC pass/fail behaviour against actual mail flow. Validates that *published* policy and *enforced* policy match.
Findings: - **Info** (CWE-200) — banner discloses MTA software + version. - **Medium** (CWE-1104) — known-stale MTA (Sendmail, Exim < 4.95, Postfix 1.x/2.x, Exchange 6.x). - **Medium** (CWE-345) — sample mail's `Authentication-Results` show `spf=fail` / `dkim=fail` / `dmarc=fail` — broken authentication chain.
Categories: `info_disclosure`, `vulnerable_dependency`, `authentication_bypass`.

parameter.name: domain
parameter.description: Apex domain to query MX for (e.g. "example.com").

parameter.name: sample_email_path
parameter.description: Optional path to a saved `.eml` file from the target's domain. When provided, the file's `Authentication-Results` header is parsed for real-world SPF / DKIM / DMARC pass/fail behaviour against actual mail flow.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.description: Per-connect SMTP timeout in seconds. Default 5.

returns.description: {success, domain, mx_records, mx_results: [{preference, host, success, banner, ehlo_response, software, version, flags}], sample_mail: {success, headers_present, spf, dkim, dmarc, ...} | None}.
